own_scenes.desc: Fab 5 Freddy (Fred Brathwaite), del grupo de grafiteros de Brooklyn Fabulous 5 con Lee Quiñones, ofrecía en The Village Voice murales por encargo; con Michael Holman montó la Canal Zone Party (1979), donde apareció Jean-Michel Basquiat, mitad de SAMO, y llevó a Bambaataa al Mudd Club. La Zulu Nation y los Funky 4 + 1, que mezclaban punk y hip hop ante los Beastie Boys, bajaron al Ritz, el Mudd Club, Danceteria, Negril y el Roxy de Kool Lady Blue: en Negril, cedido por el mánager de los Clash, se juntaron por primera vez los cuatro elementos; en el Roxy, una pista de patinaje de la calle 18, Bambaataa, Afrika Islam y Grand Mixer D.ST pinchaban para Bianca Jagger, Warhol, la Rock Steady Crew o Madonna. Debbie Harry y Chris Stein (Blondie), amigos de Flash, nombraron a Freddy y a Flash en «Rapture» (1981), primer rap número 1 en Billboard, y llevaron a los Funky 4 + 1 a Saturday Night Live (14 de febrero de 1981), primera actuación de hip hop en la televisión nacional. Para Holman, sin el abrazo del downtown el hip hop no habría sido lo que fue; para Dante Ross, los negros se llevaron pantalones pitillo y opiáceos y los blancos toda esa cultura.

refs.q: Arguably, it’s the first hip-hop club in history for that reason, Negril.
refs.para: Michael Holman (journalist/​filmmaker/​creator, Graffiti Rock): So, at that gig in ’81 for Bow Wow Wow, Ruza Blue [also known as Kool Lady Blue] knew Malcolm McLaren. Kosmo Vinyl, who was the manager of the Clash, he was given Thursday night at a little club in the East Village called Negril, a Jamaican reggae club, to do whatever he wanted. He’s too busy, so he gives it to Ruza Blue. She sees my hip-hop revue opening up for Bow Wow Wow and asked me to bring that to her club at Negril. Now, for the first time, there is a hip-hop club where all the elements of hip-hop—writing, dancing, turntablism, and spitting rhymes—happens. Arguably, it’s the first hip-hop club in history for that reason, Negril.

refs.q: It was freedom. Musical freedom, no segregation, no color lines.
refs.para: Afrika Islam (DJ, producer): It was freedom. Musical freedom, no segregation, no color lines. Rich, poor. Bianca Jagger to Andy Warhol to the Rock Steady Crew to Grandmaster Flash to Hall & Oates to Herbie Hancock to Madonna to Afrika Islam. Kool Lady Blue put together a melting pot.

refs.q: What put rap music on the map was when the culture was encapsulated as a multifaceted diamond of dance, writing, song, music, lyrics, visuals, graffiti, and then presented to the world.
refs.para: I’m willing to wager that if hip-hop had depended only on the Sugarhill Gang’s breakout song, and it had not come downtown and experienced the cultural and media embrace and explosion, it would not have happened the way it did. What put rap music on the map was when the culture was encapsulated as a multifaceted diamond of dance, writing, song, music, lyrics, visuals, graffiti, and then presented to the world.
